Alternatively, they proposed that cycling has greater biomechanical similarities to multi-joint free weight exercise compared to running and therefore may have provided a greater transfer of training. Counterintuitively, Panissa and colleagues (61) reported that high-intensity aerobic cycling negatively affected strength to a greater degree than high-intensity treadmill running when performed immediately before a resistance training bout. Over time, this would likely have a detrimental impact on hypertrophy as a result of chronic reductions in mechanical tension.
